headline: Nebius, a company that rents out computing power for AI, has bought the startup Inferize, whose software is meant to get AI models ready to serve customers faster.
score_reason: Small, price-undisclosed acquisition that adds to Nebius's string of software purchases; the benefits are the companies' own claims.
importance_line: Companies that pay Nebius to run AI models may get extra capacity ready faster, and Nebius adds to its earlier purchase of Eigen AI, but the price was not disclosed and the speed gains are the companies' own claims.
summary: SDxCentral reports that Nebius has acquired Inferize, a startup founded this year by the people behind Granulate, a software-optimization firm that Intel bought in 2022, and will fold its technology into Nebius' Token Factory service for running AI models. Nebius says the technology cuts "cold starts", the time a model needs to load before answering its first request, so each GPU (AI chip) can serve more customers; the price was not disclosed.
